messages:
sophia: Heads-up: prod token/sec on the continuous batcher dropped ~28% after the 09:12 deploy. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/ctb/instances/42 :token_down:

ajay: Saw the alert. CI perf job flagged the merge too — infra-bot says `ci/perf/ctb-checker` failed with -3.2% tokens/sec on main@9f3a7c.

taylor: Starting a bisect now. My gut says the scheduler window/prefetch change from PR #4123 — launching local canaries.

lina: KV cache hit rate on affected hosts dropped from ~82% -> ~64% around the same time. From kafka logs: `kv_cache.hitrate=0.64 prefetched=1.1k`.

ajay: Profiler dump shows memcpy and scheduler poll hot:

```
# perf top -p <ctb-pid>
  memcpy_avx       34.1%
  scheduler_poll   21.3%
  kv_cache_lookup  12.6%
  kernel_select    8.7%
```

Sophia: Kernel selection logs show fallback to a memcpy-heavy path for long sequences. Looks like `kernel.policy=auto` chose `generic_memcopy` after the prefetch tweak.

```
[2026-03-18T09:12:34Z] kernel.select: chosen=generic_memcopy reason=prefetch_miss seq=2048
```

taylor: Quick experiment: forcing `kernel.preference=fast_attention` locally recovers ~+22% tokens/sec. Command I used: `rbctl rollout set --env=canary kernel.preference=fast_attention`.

ajay: Forcing kernel helps but doesn't explain kv hitrate drop. Batch sizes increased on prod (avg batch_size from 6 -> 18) which could cause more KV churn.

lina: Batcher trace shows `continuous_batcher.window` effectively increased after the scheduler changes; coalescing more requests into bigger batches. Example trace: `window=80ms -> batch_size=18` after merge. We should try reducing window/backpressure.

sophia: Proposed action plan:
1) Roll back the scheduler window change (PR #4123) on canary immediately.
2) Hotfix: pin `kernel.preference=fast_attention` in prod until we stabilize.
3) Run an A/B: keep original window (40ms) vs current (80ms) and measure kv_hitrate and tokens/sec.

taylor: I've opened a revert PR: #4138 titled "revert: scheduler window prefetchtweak" and queued it for immediate canary rollback. Also preparing hotfix `hotfix/kernel-pin` for prod.

infra-bot: deploy started: hotfix/kernel-pin -> prod nodes [gpu-01,gpu-02,gpu-03,gpu-04,gpu-05,gpu-06,gpu-07,gpu-08,gpu-09,gpu-10,gpu-11,gpu-12].

ajay: Re-run the perf/regression job after hotfix finishes. If tokens/sec recovers then the scheduler change is most likely root cause. We should also add a CI guard for this pattern.

lina: I'll add a CI perf check: fail the job if tokens/sec drops >2% or kv_cache.hitrate drops >5% relative to baseline. Also creating a small synthetic test that simulates long sequences + warm KV.

sophia: Thanks team. I'll watch the dashboards and post a follow-up in ~10m. If canary rollback settles, we can coordinate a measured re-intro with a smaller window and a KV warmup step. :eyes:
